questions.question: On average, how many words per day does a person write by hand?
questions.answer: 100 - Most people write roughly 100 words by hand daily in notes, forms, or messages.

questions.question: True or False: Typing is generally faster than handwriting for most people.
questions.answer: True - Average typing speed is around 40 words per minute, while handwriting averages 20 words per minute.

questions.question: Which country first introduced cursive handwriting in schools?
questions.answer: France - Cursive was standardized in French schools in the 17th century.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of handwritten letters are never opened by the recipient?
questions.answer: 25% - Studies suggest about one in four handwritten letters are overlooked.

questions.question: True or False: Handwriting activates different brain areas than typing.
questions.answer: True - Handwriting engages fine motor skills and memory-related brain regions more than typing.

questions.question: Which age group is most likely to prefer handwriting over typing?
questions.answer: Children - Many studies show young learners benefit from writing by hand for learning letters and words.

questions.question: True or False: People with messy handwriting tend to have higher IQs.
questions.answer: False - Messy handwriting does not correlate with intelligence; legibility is unrelated to IQ.

questions.question: How many letters are in the longest known handwritten manuscript?
questions.answer: 3,000,000 - The longest handwritten manuscripts, like religious texts, can reach millions of letters.

questions.question: True or False: Learning cursive can improve fine motor skills in children.
questions.answer: True - Studies show cursive improves coordination, dexterity, and brain activation.

questions.question: Which of these modern tools helps most people practice handwriting today?
questions.answer: Tablets with stylus - Digital styluses allow handwriting practice in classrooms and at home.
